title: Cube: scramble generation and initial state
description:
How to set up a scrambled cube for solving.

## Solved initial state
54 stickers: 9 per face, each face one color.
Components: white, yellow, red, orange, blue, green (or W/Y/R/O/B/G)
Each sticker is a component instance placed on its home face grid.

## Scramble methods

### Option A: Random move sequence
Apply N random moves from the 18-move set (WCA uses 20+ moves for competition scrambles). This is the standard approach and guarantees a reachable state.

### Option B: Server-generated scramble
Server uses its ChaCha20Rng to generate a scramble sequence at room creation. The scramble is applied as a series of perturber effects during setup phase.

### Option C: Client-provided scramble
Client sends a scramble string (e.g. "R U R' F2 D'") in the room creation request. Server applies it.

## Recommendation
Option B for competitive/server use (deterministic, auditable via RNG seed).
Option C for practice (player enters a known scramble).
Option A is what Option B does internally.

## Initial setup
The game definition's setup phase:
1. Place all 54 stickers in solved position
2. Apply scramble (server action)
3. Game begins

## Move counter
Track move count for speedcubing. The engine already has move_count.

## WCA compliance (stretch)
WCA scrambles use specific algorithms (Kociemba's, random state). This is out of scope for initial implementation — random move sequences are sufficient.

## Test
Generate a 20-move scramble, apply to solved cube, verify cube is scrambled (not solved). Apply the inverse sequence, verify cube is solved again.
